about: Every platform adapter declares itself here before an executor exists. Effect class and reversibility belong to the action, not the platform: an unlisted upload and a public reply come from the same adapter and are not the same kind of act. Order is activation order, cheapest-to-undo first; the registry refuses a file whose order contradicts its own risk ranking.

platforms.notes: First adapter: two of its five actions are revocable, so it is the right place to prove one real outbound action end to end. Executor refuses without owner OAuth credentials. Enabled today: the three reversible actions only. reply_comment and moderate_comment are declared but disabled until a reversible action has actually run end to end.

actions.name: upload_video:unlisted
actions.notes: Deliberately narrowed: only unlisted uploads are declared. A public upload is not in the allowlist and has to be added by editing this file.

actions.name: reply_comment
actions.notes: A reply is visible to third parties the moment it posts. Deleting it afterwards does not unread it, which is why the action carries the harder class rather than the adapter.

actions.name: moderate_comment
actions.notes: Holding or removing someone else's comment cannot be undone from their side of the exchange.

platforms.notes: Own domain, but delivery cannot be recalled once it leaves. Declared only: no executor, and nothing is allowlisted until one exists.
Paid API tier with a per-post cost, so the quota ceiling is declared before the executor.
Direct post requires platform app approval before the endpoint is usable, so this entry documents a gate we cannot yet cross.
Requires a business account and app review. Last in order because the effect is public and permanent and the credential path is the longest.
